An extension (Form IN-151, filable at myVTax) extends the filing deadline to Oct. 15, 2026 but does NOT extend the time to pay — late payment penalty and interest accrue after the April due date, and a $50 late-file penalty applies if the return is not filed by the extended Oct. 15, 2026 date.
_strings.@@60bf67d4e06d: Treaty conformity — VT conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from VT income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the VT return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Vermont's resident return starts from federal adjusted gross income and does NOT add back federally treaty-exempt income; it explicitly SUBTRACTS it. Form IN-111 Line 1 is 'Federal Adjusted Gross Income REQUIRED entry. Enter the amount from your federal Form 1040 or, if applicable, from the recomputed federal Form 1040' (2025 IN-111 Instructions). The DOR 'Resident' page states: 'If you are a Vermont resident, your income starts with federal adjusted gross income minus the following: Income exempted from state taxation by the laws of the United States...'. Line 2 (Net Modifications to Federal AGI, from Schedule IN-112, Part I, Line 19) contains the standard state additions/subtractions — non-Vermont state/local obligation interest and federal bonus depreciation as additions; U.S.-obligation interest, the capital-gains exclusion, the retirement-income exemption, medical expenses, state/local taxes, railroad retirement, and military retirement/survivor benefits as subtractions — with no treaty-income add-back. Because treaty-exempt income is already excluded from federal AGI and is additionally listed as a Vermont subtraction (not an addition), it is not re-taxed -> conforms = true.

state_tax.work_common_tail: . Tax line: Form IN-111, Line 8: 'Vermont Income Tax' — tax on Vermont Taxable Income (Line 7) from the 2025 tax table or the applicable 2025 rate schedule; if federal AGI (Line 1) is greater than $150,000, Line 8 is the GREATER of (1) 3% of federal AGI less interest from U.S. obligations or (2) the rate-schedule calculation. Line 7 'Vermont Taxable Income. Line 3 minus Line 6. If less than zero, enter -0-', where Line 3 = Line 1 federal AGI + Line 2 net modifications (Schedule IN-112, Part I, Line 19) and Line 6 = Line 4 Vermont standard deduction + Line 5e personal exemption deduction. This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: TY2025 re-indexation: the four rates are unchanged (3.35/6.60/7.60/8.75%) but every dollar figure moved — Schedule X 49,400/119,700/249,700 (was 47,900/116,000/242,000), Y-1 82,500/199,450/304,000 (was 79,950/193,300/294,600), Y-2 exactly half Y-1 at 41,250/99,725/152,000, Z 66,200/171,000/276,850 (was 64,200/165,700/268,300); standard deduction 7,650/15,300/7,650/11,450 (was 7,400/14,850/7,400/11,100); the additional standard deduction per federal box rose to $1,250 (was $1,200) and its birth-date test moved to 'born before Jan. 2, 1961'; the personal exemption rose to $5,300 (was $5,100). Two-pass sourcing (2025): pass 1 = the 2025 Form IN-111 Instructions' printed '2025 Vermont Tax Rate Schedules' (p.12); pass 2 = the INDEPENDENT 2025 GB-1210 withholding booklet's Vermont Percentage Method ANNUAL PAYROLLS table, whose bounds net of the built-in offsets ($3,825 single, $11,475 married) reproduce Schedule X and Y-1 exactly and whose UNROUNDED constants (1,654.90 / 6,294.70 / 16,174.70 and 2,763.75 / 10,482.45 / 18,428.25) equal the exact cumulative bracket sums this engine computes. Unlike TY2024, direct https fetches of tax.vermont.gov succeeded with a browser User-Agent, so both documents are live official copies rather than Wayback captures. Printed-constant divergence: the schedules' 'VT Base Tax' constants are whole-dollar roundings of the exact cumulative sums (Y-1 at 82,500 prints 2,764.00 vs exact 2,763.75; X at 49,400 prints 1,655.00 vs exact 1,654.90; Y-2 at 152,000 prints 9,214.00 vs exact 9,214.125; Z at 66,200 prints 2,218.00 vs exact 2,217.70), so form arithmetic using the printed constants can differ from this op's exact marginal math by up to $1. The booklet's own $85,000 MFJ example prints $2,929 and exact math also gives $2,928.75 -> $2,929, so they agree there. Base guidance: supply Form IN-111, Line 3 'Federal Adjusted Gross Income with Modifications' = Line 1 federal AGI (federal Form 1040, Line 11a — the 2025 IN-111 face cites Line 11a) plus/minus Line 2 net modifications to federal AGI (Schedule IN-112, Part I, Line 19 — note the 2025 line number; it was Line 18 on the 2024 schedule). With no Vermont modifications, Line 3 equals federal AGI, so plain federal AGI is the correct input for most filers. The op then subtracts the shipped 2025 Vermont standard deduction (IN-111 Line 4) and $5,300 per exemption (Lines 5a-5e) to reproduce Line 7, Vermont Taxable Income. Tax-table mandate below $75,000: each 2025 Vermont Tax Rate Schedule prints 'TAXABLE INCOME UNDER $75,000 USE THE TAX TABLES' across its sub-$75,000 rows. The 2025 Vermont Tax Tables (IN-111 Instr. pp.13-17) compute tax at the MIDPOINT of each $100 band using the schedules' PRINTED (rounded) base-tax constants, then round to whole dollars — spot-verified: the Single $25,000-$25,100 band prints $839 (3.35% x $25,050 = $839.175) where exact math at $25,000 gives $837.50; the $30,000-$30,100 band prints $1,007; the $74,900-$75,000 band prints Single $3,341 / MFJ $2,511 / MFS $3,606 / HoH $2,796, and the HoH figure only reproduces from the PRINTED $2,218.00 constant ($2,218.00 + 6.6% x $8,750 = $2,795.50 -> $2,796), not from the exact $2,217.70. Bracket math therefore differs from the table by a few dollars inside a band; the filed form must use the table below $75,000. CRITICAL - 3% minimum tax not modeled: 2025 IN-111 Instr. Line 8: 'Taxpayers who have a federal Adjusted Gross Income (AGI) greater than $150,000 must pay a minimum Vermont tax of 3% of federal AGI. If your federal AGI, Line 1, is greater than $150,000, enter the amount that is higher: 1) 3% of your federal AGI less interest from U.S. obligations, or 2) tax calculated on Vermont Taxable Income, Line 7, using the applicable tax rate schedule.' This op computes only (2); when the 3% floor binds (typically large modifications/deductions relative to AGI), plain bracket math understates Line 8. The printed schedules break a row at exactly $75,000 solely to flag the tax-table mandate — the rate does NOT change at $75,000 (e.g. MFJ 3.35% actually runs $0-$82,500; Single 6.60% runs $49,400-$119,700; MFS 6.60% runs $41,250-$99,725; HoH 6.60% runs $66,200-$171,000). Same-rate rows are merged in the shipped brackets; the math is identical. Qualifying Widow(er)/surviving spouse: Schedule Y-1 is captioned 'Married Filing Jointly; Qualifying Widow(er); or Civil Union Filing Jointly' and the 2025 standard-deduction chart gives Qualifying Widow(er) the same $15,300 as MFJ, so the engine's QSS-to-MFJ mapping matches Vermont exactly. Civil Union Filing Separately uses Schedule Y-2 (married_filing_separately); Civil Union Filing Jointly uses Y-1. Additional standard deduction not applied by the engine: $1,250 per standard-deduction box checked on federal Form 1040 (born before Jan. 2, 1961, or blind) is added to the Line 4 standard deduction per the 2025 chart — Single 8,900/10,150 for 1/2 boxes; MFJ or QW 16,550/17,800/19,050/20,300 for 1/2/3/4 boxes; MFS 8,900/10,150/11,400/12,650; HoH 12,700/13,950. Compute those cases from the form's chart. Exemption gates not modeled: Line 5a counts yourself ONLY if no one can claim you as a dependent on a 2025 return; Line 5b (spouse/civil union partner) must be left blank if filing status is Qualifying Widow(er) or Married Filing Separately. Vermont has no itemized-deduction option on the 2025 IN-111 — Line 4 offers only the Vermont standard deduction (there is no itemized line on the form). Steps between Line 8 and the final Line 14 'Vermont Income Tax' are NOT modeled: Line 9 Net Adjustment to Vermont Tax (Schedule IN-119 Part I — additions such as recapture of a Vermont tax credit and 24% of additional federal tax on qualified retirement plan/IRA/HSA/MSA distributions, federal Investment Tax Credit recapture, and Form 4972 lump-sum distributions; subtractions such as the Credit for the Elderly or the Disabled, the Vermont-based portion of the Investment Tax Credit, and the Farm Income Averaging Credit), and Lines 11-13 the Tax Deductible Charitable Contribution — despite the caption, the 2025 instructions describe it as a nonrefundable tax CREDIT equal to 5% of the first $20,000 of qualifying charitable contributions (max $1,000, Line 13) subtracted from tax on Line 14, not an income deduction. Part-year residents and nonresidents: Line 15 income adjustment percentage (Schedule IN-113, Line 35) multiplies Line 14 to get Line 16 Adjusted Vermont Income Tax — not modeled; full-year residents enter 100%. Line 21 Child Care Contribution (CCC) — NOT modeled; an additional amount on Form IN-111 beside the income tax, in its first full year (the line and Act 76 of 2023 are recorded as the TY2024 law change in the 2024 pack). 2025 IN-111 Instructions, Line 21 (p. 8): 'Act 76 of 2023, an act relating to child care, early education, workers' compensation, and unemployment insurance, created a child care contribution (CCC) in Vermont. Per the statutory directive, collection of the CCC commenced on July 1, 2024. Individuals with self-employment income from Vermont sources earned on July 1, 2024, or after must include their CCC on Form IN-111.' The 2025 CHILD CARE CONTRIBUTION WORKSHEET ('Complete this worksheet if you have self-employment income reported on federal Form 1040, Schedule SE') has four lines: 1 'Enter the amount from federal Form 1040, Schedule SE, Line 6'; 2 the part of it 'earned for work performed outside of Vermont'; 3 = line 1 minus line 2; 4 'Multiply Line 3 by 0.11% (0.0011). Enter this amount on Form IN-111, Line 21' — the 2024 worksheet's half-year exclusion (its lines 4-5, income earned before July 1, 2024) is gone. No threshold or cap is printed; GB-1326 (October 2024): 'unlike federal self-employment taxes, there is no cap on self-employment income subject to the CCC', and the CCC 'applies to all self-employment income earned by Vermont residents and nonresidents for work physically performed in Vermont'. Statute: 32 V.S.A. chapter 246, § 10553(b) 'The contribution rate shall be 0.44 percent of each employee's covered wages and 0.11 percent on each self-employed individual's self-employment income' (added by Act 76 of 2023, § 24, eff. July 1, 2024); § 10553(a)(2) collects the self-employed share 'as if the contributions were Vermont income tax subject to the estimated payment requirements of 32 V.S.A. chapter 151, subchapter 5'. Line 23 Total Vermont Taxes: 'Add Lines 20 through 22 and enter result.' FARMER / FISHERMAN box — the last box of the page-1 'Check all that apply' row (AMENDED, CANNABIS, RECOMPUTED, EXTENDED, FARMER / FISHERMAN), on the form since TY2024; NOT modeled. 2025 IN-111 Instructions, Farmer/Fisherman (p. 6): 'If you meet the definition of a qualified farmer or fisherman under 26 U.S.C. § 6654(i)(2), please check the box on Form IN-111. Generally, a qualified farmer or fisherman must earn at least 2/3 of their gross income from farming or fishing in either the current or proceeding tax year to be exempt from paying quarterly estimated taxes. Please see IRS Topic No. 416 for more information' ('proceeding' as printed). The booklet says only to check the box; its Line 31 (underpayment interest and penalty) text prints no farmer or fisherman exception — 'Estimated tax payments must either be: 1) equal to 100% of last year's tax liability OR 2) 90% of this year's tax liability. If the tax liability due, less withholding, is less than $500, you will not be subject to penalty or interest charges.' — so what the box changes on Worksheet IN-152 is not documented there.
